21:26 Local Time, 11:26 GMT, 16:56 IST: England’s T20I stocks continue to soar under Harry Brook’s leadership, having lost just four of the 30 matches played under his captaincy. After narrowly going down in the series opener in Melbourne, England have bounced back emphatically, outclassing Australia in the next two games to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. Tonight, the star of the show was Jamie Overton, who claimed a five-wicket haul to dismantle Australia's batting line-up and bowl them out for just 108 in the first innings. That was never going to be enough to trouble England. There were a couple of rain interruptions during the chase as Phil Salt departed early, while Brook also failed to make much of an impact with the bat. But Aneurin Donald was once again a treat to watch, smashing 32 off just 13 deliveries. Riley Meredith picked up all three wickets to fall, but Jordan Cox and Tom Banton comfortably mopped up the remaining runs to take England over the line.
--Australia’s second defeat in nine completed T20Is at the Gabba, ending a five-match winning streak. Their only previous loss came against West Indies in 2013.

Harry Brook (England captain): [On the win] Unbelievable effort from the boys. I thought Jamie Overton was absolutely outstanding tonight. He's worked hard over the last couple of weeks, put in a little bit of extra graft at training yesterday and really simplified his game. He reaped the rewards tonight. [On setting up the Australian batters] Yeah, and that's just part of cricket, trying to figure out what the best mode of dismissal on that surface is. I know it's a short format and you try to hit the ball to all parts, but he (Overton) was bowling on a string. It felt like he could just set a slightly different field and make the batters make a mistake. [On the opportunity to seal the series in Sydney] It would be a phenomenal effort from everybody to come over here and beat a strong Australian side in their own backyard. It would be lovely to finish it off in Sydney. But we've got to stay in the moment, stay present and see what's in front of us.

England are yet to lose a T20I series under Harry Brook and have a chance to extend that impressive record when they take the field in Sydney on Sunday for the fourth T20I.
